notes: Slice is thin on checkable groups with their own websites, and the search budget ran out (6 of 6 used). Three records written. Dropped with reasons: Cathedral Park CDC (broad area 'West Philadelphia', programs listed with no schedules, no way to join or volunteer), Calvary Center for Culture and Community (a community space with no address, contact details or dated content; looks like a venue, so likely not_a_group), Carroll Park Community Council (a 2012 search snippet says it closed for lack of funding; source not read, so not published as defunct). Could not read: the city's April 2026 registered community organization PDF (the fetch returned only link annotations), and the park friends list (an interactive map with no text). Domains that did not resolve on 2026-10-08: noah19151.com and opca19151.org. A TLS certificate error on overbrookfarmsclub.org. Search summaries disagreed on Council district lines (one said Haddington and Overbrook sit in District 4; West Philly neighborhoods sit in District 3); I did not verify district boundaries. Business associations (Lancaster Avenue, City Avenue, Haverford Avenue, Lansdowne Avenue) were not recorded because they are not community programs. Mill Creek and Dunlap search found no current civic association; Dunlap was not checked further. Walnut Hill's membership is the only paid join path found in this slice; the other records are free or unknown.

records.name: Mill Creek Urban Farm
records.summary: A farm on Brown Street in West Philadelphia that grows produce without chemicals and teaches farm classes for all ages. It also runs a farmers market.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the farm through the volunteer form (wear a hat and protective boots), help at the market, or ask about a group visit.

schedule.text: Farmers market on Saturdays from noon to 2 pm at 49th and Brown streets. The same page also says the market is coming soon, so confirm before going. Volunteer days are not published.

cost.text: Prices are not listed. The market accepts FMNP vouchers.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the farm's site, email millcreekfarmphilly@gmail.com, or visit the Saturday market.
first_step.basis: The market is open to visitors, and the site lists a volunteer form and an email address.

records.notes: The site shows no dated events and no year. It says 'Farmers Market Coming Soon!' while also giving Saturday market hours, so confirm the market before a visitor relies on it. The mailing address is a PO box in 19151. The farm is a program of A LittleTaste of Everything, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.
